claims.text: This trip was booked as an UPFRONT_QUOTE: the fare was fixed at SGD 10.00 (quoted_fare_sgd) on the fare ledger, yet the same ledger records a charged_total of SGD 12.00. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider recovers in full the amount by which the charged total exceeds the quoted fare plus only those pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and the ledger's own derived money block publishes that excess as '2.00'. The rider's claim is therefore an arithmetic claim against the quote, not a demand for a discretionary goodwill payment.

The whole SGD 2.00 excess is a single ERP line for the gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)', and that line does not lie on the booked route. The fare ledger's erp_gantries entry carries on_optimal_route = false, and the derived money block splits the ERP totals as on_optimal_route_total 0.00 against off_optimal_route_total 2.00. Pass-through charges are only properly chargeable to the rider where they are costs of the route the rider booked; this one is not.

POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of the gantry as a crossing. The nearest of the 73 sampled fixes to this gantry is 6,778.01 m away - roughly twenty-seven times the crossing radius - and gap_brackets_closest_approach is false, so the vehicle never passed the gantry at all. The ledger states the same conclusion in terms, marking the line 'crossed': false with the reason that the trace's closest approach is further away than the POL-RD-09(4) crossing radius.

The ledger's own properly_chargeable computation already applies that conclusion: erp_lines[0].crossed is false, erp_total is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00 and waiting_time_fee is 0.00, so properly_chargeable.total is 0.00 and pol_rd_11_remedy is 2.00 with pol_rd_11_remedy_available true. There is nothing for the platform to set off against the refund.

The rider's entitlement does not depend on proving a route deviation. The trace in fact shows no material detour - excess is 0.18 km, or 4.6%, below both POL-RD-01 thresholds - and on an upfront-quoted trip no distance-or-time refund is available whatever the excess under POL-RD-11. POL-RD-09(4) expressly makes the phantom-gantry correction available 'whether or not a deviation exists', which is exactly this case: the rider is not asking for the detour remedy, only for the line he never owed.

The driver's own account on the file is that the meter adds ERP automatically when he selects it and that he 'might have pressed it by mistake' - an admission that the line was not earned - and nothing in the case contradicts it: neither the trip record nor the 73 GPS fixes places the vehicle anywhere on the CTE corridor at the 21:47:40 charge time. An admitted mistaken selection with no trace of a crossing is a billing error on its face.

No external cause can rescue this line. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00521-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0) and carries no payload: no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no advisory can be matched to the route. I disclose the artifact's impairment expressly - the absence is itself citable, and the absence of any advisory means an unchallenged, uncrossed gantry line stands unexplained by anything but the driver's own mistaken selection.

This is not a case for escalation. POL-RD-09(4) provides that the counterpart-tracing trigger in POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged where the only unmatched line is one refunded under that limb, and the single off-route ERP line here is precisely that line. A knowable, matchable, plainly erroneous charge is to be ruled on and refunded, not referred.

The pass-through finding rests on clean evidence. The GPS trace is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0, 100% coverage, 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence and no gaps at all (max_gap_sec 0.0), so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), and the confidence cap that POL-GEN-02 sets on the deciding artifact is 1.0. The rider's showing is not carried by down-weighted material.

The rider carries no corroboration burden beyond the trace. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far below the POL-RD-08 threshold of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated that would require corroboration beyond the gps_trace. This rider has not been making unsupported deviation claims.

Because the phantom line is the whole of the disputed SGD 2.00 and POL-RD-09(4) refunds such a line in full as a standalone correction, the entire contested amount is returned to the rider. On POL-GEN-03's party-relative vocabulary that is a full refund of the filing party's claim, together with a billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) which records the defect without suppressing the money.

claims.text: POL-RD-01's numeric gate fails on this trip's own trace, so no deviation exists however the rider frames it. The measured excess is 0.18 km, or 4.6% of the 3.9 km optimal, and POL-RD-01 requires BOTH that the excess exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms AND that it exceed 20% of optimal before a deviation is ESTABLISHED. Neither limb is met, and POL-RD-01 says in terms that if either establishment test fails the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 expressly makes the trace figure govern: where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs and the trip record's rounded copy 'may NOT be cited for the threshold test'. The trace records 4.08 km over the 3.9 km optimal, and it is a clean measurement - 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s - so there is no reading of the record on which the excess approaches either threshold.

POL-RD-08 places the initial burden on the rider and requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold before the burden shifts to the driver. The rider has shown no such excess - 0.18 km and 4.6% - so the burden never shifts at all: the driver is never put to invoking POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12, and no exculpatory clause even needs to be reached.

fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 10.00, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run: no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the excess is characterised, and the rider is already whole on those lines. The rider's own words - 'ten dollar fixed price' - are the upfront quote, and under this fare model any detour cost falls on the driver, not on the rider.

Stripping the framing away, the whole contested sum is one ERP line and nothing else: charged_total 12.00 less quoted_fare 10.00 is exactly 2.00, and fare_breakdown.tolls_erp is 2.00, so there is no distance or time overcharge inside the contested amount at all. On an upfront trip POL-RD-11(a) leaves the rider only the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and no distance remedy attaches to the ROUTE_DEVIATION category on this record.

Nothing here fires a POL-RD-10 trigger, so the case is decidable on the record rather than escalatable: the trace meets POL-RD-07's integrity test (no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, cadence 10 s throughout, POL-RD-07 therefore not engaged); the trip identifier TRP-00521 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the timestamps run forward and agree; and the only unmatched charge line is the ERP line itself, which POL-RD-09(4) and POL-RD-10(8) both expressly exclude from the unmatched-line trigger.

The driver does not resist the 2.00 ERP line, and on this record cannot: the trace's closest approach to the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry is 6,778 m, far outside the 250 m POL-RD-09(4) crossing radius, so the line cannot stand as a crossed gantry and a 2.00 correction is due under POL-RD-09(4) - or equally under POL-RD-11(a)'s 'ERP actually crossed'. That correction is the ceiling and no more: it carries no distance or time refund, no POL-RD-06 uplift (there is no material deviation to uplift), and no escalation, because POL-RD-09(4) is a standalone billing-integrity correction and not a finding against the driver's routing on this trip.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the whole of the SGD 2.00 you contested is returned to you, and both advocates agree it should be. This was an upfront-quoted trip (fare_breakdown.fare_model = UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd = SGD 10.00) on which you were charged charged_total = SGD 12.00. The entire SGD 2.00 difference is a single ERP line (fare_breakdown.tolls_erp = SGD 2.00) for the gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)'. That line does not stand: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00521) is complete and clean — 73 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — and its closest approach to the gantry is 6,778 m, roughly twenty-seven times the 250 m POL-RD-09(4) crossing radius, with gap_brackets_closest_approach false. The ledger itself marks the line 'crossed': false and on_optimal_route = false, splitting on_optimal_route_total 0.00 against off_optimal_route_total 2.00. Under POL-RD-09(4) a gantry charge the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists, and POL-RD-10(8) is expressly not triggered by a line refunded under that limb. The same result follows under POL-RD-11(a): your remedy is charged_total less quoted_fare_sgd less the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09; properly_chargeable.total is SGD 0.00 (erp_total 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00), so the amount is SGD 12.00 − SGD 10.00 = SGD 2.00, equal to the published pol_rd_11_remedy of 2.00. Because the whole contested sum is returned, the outcome is FULL_REFUND. No distance remedy is added on top and none is double-counted: POL-RD-11(a) and POL-RD-09(4) are the same SGD 2.00, stated once.

On the routing question, nothing is owed either way. The measured excess is 0.18 km, or 4.6% of the 3.9 km optimal (trace_distance_km 4.08 against optimal_distance_km 3.9), below both POL-RD-01 thresholds of 0.8 km and 20%, so no deviation is established and the outcome is not one 'however the rider characterises the trip'. In any event this is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: no distance-or-time refund is available regardless of the excess. The two advocates' characterisations of the SGD 2.00 — billing correction (driver) versus full refund of the contested amount (rider) — come to the same figure, and that figure is awarded.

To the driver: your own account on the file — that the meter adds ERP automatically when you select it and that you 'might have pressed it by mistake' — is an admission against your own interest and is consistent with the trace, which places the vehicle nowhere near the CTE corridor at the 21:47:40 charge time. Nothing in the trip record or the 73 fixes supports the line. This is not a finding about your routing on this trip: no deviation was committed, and no POL-RD-06 driver-profile uplift or conduct referral arises, because POL-RD-06 requires a MATERIAL deviation and there is none. No driver compensation is due: you were billed 4.1 km against a 4.08 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall.

Credibility and confidence: the finding rests on EV-FARE-00521 and EV-GPS-00521, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap on confidence is 1.0 and the ruling sits at 0.95. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00521-01 (status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0) carries no fact and the ruling does not rely on it; its absence is noted and is not an escalation trigger, because no exculpatory traffic clause was invoked against it — no party asserted an external traffic cause for any measured deviation, so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-13 are not in play and POL-RD-10(5) does not fire. The GPS trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), trip identifier TRP-00521 matches across the trip record, trace and ledger, the timestamps run forward and agree, and the only unmatched charge line is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4) — so no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires and a monetary ruling issues.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 ERP line for gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' on TRP-00521 was charged for a line the GPS trace never crossed, so it is a phantom charge. It has been refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction; review the ERP selection on this trip (the driver's statement records a possible mistaken selection) as a billing-integrity matter.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the disputed sum is the SGD 2.00 'ERP' line on a SGD 12.00 card charge against a SGD 10.00 upfront quote. I rule a FULL_REFUND of SGD 2.00 to the rider, with a billing-integrity referral that does not delay the money.

Why the whole SGD 2.00 comes back. This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: the fare was fixed at booking at SGD 10.00 (fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd = 10.00) and the card was charged SGD 12.00 (fare_breakdown.charged_total = 12.00). The entire difference is the single ERP line of SGD 2.00 (fare_breakdown.tolls_erp = 2.00). Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider recovers the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote, less only those pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. This line is not properly chargeable. The only gantry charged is 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)'; it is not on the booked optimal route (fare_breakdown.erp_gantries on_optimal_route = false, off_optimal_route_total 2.00 against on_optimal_route_total 0.00), and the vehicle never passed it — the closest of the trace's 73 fixes is 6,778.01 m away against the POL-RD-09(4) 250 m crossing radius, and gap_brackets_closest_approach is false. The ledger reaches the same conclusion: properly_chargeable.total is SGD 0.00 and its own pol_rd_11_remedy is SGD 2.00. That makes this a phantom gantry line, refundable in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not a deviation exists. 12.00 − 10.00 − 0.00 = 2.00, already a multiple of SGD 0.05.

On the routing itself there is no deviation, and nothing in this ruling rests on the driver having taken a wrong route. The trace records 4.08 km against a 3.9 km optimal — an excess of 0.18 km, or 4.6% — below both POL-RD-01 thresholds (0.8 km and 20%). I therefore accept the driver's POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-08 points that no deviation is established and the burden never shifts, and that on an upfront trip no distance-or-time refund arises (POL-RD-11). That does not change the outcome: the rider's entitlement is a charge-correction available independently of any deviation under POL-RD-09(4), and the driver's own advocate concedes the SGD 2.00 correction.

The driver's account — that the meter adds ERP automatically when selected and that he 'might have pressed it by mistake' — is evidence on the file, and it agrees with the trace and the ledger. No external traffic cause is asserted by anyone, so the bundle's traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00521-01, which is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), carries no fact here and nothing rests on it.

On escalation: the trace is COMPLETE and unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (73 fixes, 10 s cadence, max_gap_sec 0.0, no jumps), trip identifier TRP-00521 matches across all three instruments, timestamps run forward and agree, and the single unmatched charge line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-09(4) and POL-RD-10(8) expressly exclude from the unmatched-line trigger. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so the case is decided rather than escalated. No POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral applies, because there is no material deviation on this trip.

Confidence rests on EV-GPS-00521, EV-FARE-00521 and EV-TRIP-00521, all at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 ERP charge for gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' is a phantom line — the GPS trace never came within the POL-RD-09(4) 250 m crossing radius (closest of 73 fixes: 6,778.01 m) and the line is not on the booked optimal route (on_optimal_route = false). Refunded in full as a standalone correction and recorded as a billing-integrity finding; review the driver's ERP selection at fare entry.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides actually agree on the substance, and the record confirms it, so this is decided on the fare ledger and the trace and not on the routing question.

What was charged. This was an upfront-quoted trip (fare_breakdown.fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE). The fare was fixed at SGD 10.00 (quoted_fare_sgd) and SGD 12.00 was taken from the card (charged_total). The entire SGD 2.00 difference is one ERP line for the gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' (fare_breakdown.tolls_erp 2.00; erp_lines amount 2.00).

Why that line cannot stand. POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the GPS trace by treating any fix within 250 m of the gantry as a crossing. The nearest of the trace's 73 fixes (EV-GPS-00521, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) is 6,778.01 m from the gantry — roughly twenty-seven times the crossing radius — and gap_brackets_closest_approach is false. The vehicle never went near the gantry. The ledger's own derived block says the same: crossed = false, on_optimal_route = false, erp_total 0.00 after excluding the uncrossed line. A charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4): it is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver's own statement that the meter adds ERP when he selects it and that he 'might have pressed it by mistake' is an admission against his interest and is entirely consistent with the trace; it is treated as evidence of the thing conceded.

The deviation question both advocates raise. The trace shows an excess of only 0.18 km, or 4.6%, over the 3.9 km optimal route, below both POL-RD-01 thresholds (0.8 km and 20%), so no route deviation is established and the driver's burden under POL-RD-08 never arises. That is correct, and it is also irrelevant to the refund: POL-RD-09(4) makes the phantom-line correction available whether or not a deviation exists, and on an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-11 bars any distance-or-time refund in any event. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00521-01, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is disclosed by the rider's own claim and cannot rescue the line — no advisory is on file, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no external-cause excuse carries weight; but nothing turns on it here, because the refund rests on the uncrossed gantry, not on the routing.

The amount, read off the record. charged_total 12.00 less quoted_fare 10.00 = 2.00; properly_chargeable.total is 0.00 (erp_total 0.00 once the uncrossed line is excluded, airport_surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00); the ledger publishes pol_rd_11_remedy 2.00 with pol_rd_11_remedy_available true. The full SGD 2.00 you paid over the quote is returned to you, the rider.

Ruling. The whole contested sum is returned, so this is a FULL_REFUND of SGD 2.00 to the rider. The refund is a pass-through correction, not a finding against the driver's routing on this trip, so no driver compensation is due and none is awarded. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires (identifiers match, timestamps run forward, the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c), POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront fare, and the only unmatched line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes), so this is decided rather than escalated. Confidence rests on a clean trace at weight 1.0 and the fare ledger at weight 1.0; the cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 1.0 and no down-weighted artifact carries the finding.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity review: the SGD 2.00 ERP line for gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' was charged on an upfront-quoted trip although GPS trace EV-GPS-00521 never crossed it (nearest of 73 fixes is 6,778.01 m away, far outside the 250 m crossing radius; the ledger itself marks on_optimal_route false and crossed false). The line has been refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction and is recorded here as a billing-integrity defect.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties agree on the decisive facts, and the money follows from them. The trip was booked as an UPFRONT_QUOTE (fare_breakdown.fare_model) with quoted_fare_sgd of 10.00, and charged_total was 12.00. The entire 2.00 difference is a single ERP line — tolls_erp = 2.00 — for the gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)'. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider recovers the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus only the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09: 12.00 − (10.00 + 0.00) = 2.00, exactly the pol_rd_11_remedy of 2.00 the ledger publishes. That is the whole of the contested 2.00, so the refund is full.

There is no route deviation to refund, and both advocates say so. The trace figure governs under POL-RD-01 (gps_trace.trace_distance_km 4.08 km against optimal 3.9 km), giving an excess of 0.18 km, or 4.6% — below both POL-RD-01 thresholds (0.8 km and 20%). No deviation is established, no distance-or-time remedy attaches, and on an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-02 does not run in any event (POL-RD-11). The rider's own filing, read fairly, does not ask for a detour remedy: the complaint is that there is no gantry on a Tanjong Pagar–Tiong Bahru trip, which is the billing point.

The ERP line is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). The trace's closest fix to the gantry is 6,778.01 m away — roughly twenty-seven times the 250 m crossing radius — gap_brackets_closest_approach is false, and the ledger marks the line 'crossed': false with erp_total 0.00 and properly_chargeable.total 0.00. The driver's own statement on file, that the meter adds ERP automatically when he selects it and that he 'might have pressed it by mistake', is an admission against his own interest that the line was not earned, and nothing in the case contradicts it. POL-RD-09(4) refunds such a line in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, so the full 2.00 is returned and the finding also produces the POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral above.

The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00521-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload). No advisory covers the corridor, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no external-cause excuse carries weight (POL-RD-13). That absence decides nothing here: neither party advanced a traffic excuse, and the deviation claim fails on its own threshold regardless. The missing artifact carries no fact and does not enter the confidence.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires. Trip identifiers match (TRP-00521 across trip record, trace and ledger); timestamps run forward and agree; the trace is clean under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (73 fixes, 10 s cadence, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0); and the only unmatched charge line is the ERP line itself, which POL-RD-09(4) expressly excludes from the POL-RD-10(8) trigger. POL-RD-06 is not engaged because no material deviation exists, so no driver-conduct referral is due and no POL-RD-06(b) uplift applies. No driver compensation arises either: the charged distance (4.1 km) is not less than the trace distance (4.08 km), so the POL-RD-04 unbilled-distance shortfall test is not met.

Confidence: the deciding fact — that the gantry was never crossed — is carried by EV-GPS-00521 and EV-FARE-00521, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. I set confidence at 0.95. The rider_profile carries no corroboration burden (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0, far below the POL-RD-08 threshold), and no context-only profile field has been used as a ground of decision by either side.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 ERP line for the gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' on trip TRP-00521 was charged for a gantry the vehicle never crossed — the GPS trace's closest fix is 6,778.01 m away against the 250 m crossing radius and the fare ledger itself marks the line 'crossed': false. Record the billing-integrity defect on the fare ledger (EV-FARE-00521) so the phantom pass-through line is not re-billed. This referral rides with the refund and does not delay or displace it.

ledger.claim: This trip was booked as an UPFRONT_QUOTE: the fare was fixed at SGD 10.00 (quoted_fare_sgd) on the fare ledger, yet the same ledger records a charged_total of SGD 12.00. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider recovers in full the amount by which the charged total exceeds the quoted fare plus only those pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and the ledger's own derived money block publishes that excess as '2.00'. The rider's claim is therefore an arithmetic claim against the quote, not a demand for a discretionary goodwill payment.

The whole SGD 2.00 excess is a single ERP line for the gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)', and that line does not lie on the booked route. The fare ledger's erp_gantries entry carries on_optimal_route = false, and the derived money block splits the ERP totals as on_optimal_route_total 0.00 against off_optimal_route_total 2.00. Pass-through charges are only properly chargeable to the rider where they are costs of the route the rider booked; this one is not.

POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of the gantry as a crossing. The nearest of the 73 sampled fixes to this gantry is 6,778.01 m away - roughly twenty-seven times the crossing radius - and gap_brackets_closest_approach is false, so the vehicle never passed the gantry at all. The ledger states the same conclusion in terms, marking the line 'crossed': false with the reason that the trace's closest approach is further away than the POL-RD-09(4) crossing radius.

The ledger's own properly_chargeable computation already applies that conclusion: erp_lines[0].crossed is false, erp_total is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00 and waiting_time_fee is 0.00, so properly_chargeable.total is 0.00 and pol_rd_11_remedy is 2.00 with pol_rd_11_remedy_available true. There is nothing for the platform to set off against the refund.

The rider's entitlement does not depend on proving a route deviation. The trace in fact shows no material detour - excess is 0.18 km, or 4.6%, below both POL-RD-01 thresholds - and on an upfront-quoted trip no distance-or-time refund is available whatever the excess under POL-RD-11. POL-RD-09(4) expressly makes the phantom-gantry correction available 'whether or not a deviation exists', which is exactly this case: the rider is not asking for the detour remedy, only for the line he never owed.

The driver's own account on the file is that the meter adds ERP automatically when he selects it and that he 'might have pressed it by mistake' - an admission that the line was not earned - and nothing in the case contradicts it: neither the trip record nor the 73 GPS fixes places the vehicle anywhere on the CTE corridor at the 21:47:40 charge time. An admitted mistaken selection with no trace of a crossing is a billing error on its face.

No external cause can rescue this line. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00521-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0) and carries no payload: no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no advisory can be matched to the route. I disclose the artifact's impairment expressly - the absence is itself citable, and the absence of any advisory means an unchallenged, uncrossed gantry line stands unexplained by anything but the driver's own mistaken selection.

This is not a case for escalation. POL-RD-09(4) provides that the counterpart-tracing trigger in POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged where the only unmatched line is one refunded under that limb, and the single off-route ERP line here is precisely that line. A knowable, matchable, plainly erroneous charge is to be ruled on and refunded, not referred.

The pass-through finding rests on clean evidence. The GPS trace is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0, 100% coverage, 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence and no gaps at all (max_gap_sec 0.0), so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), and the confidence cap that POL-GEN-02 sets on the deciding artifact is 1.0. The rider's showing is not carried by down-weighted material.

The rider carries no corroboration burden beyond the trace. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far below the POL-RD-08 threshold of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated that would require corroboration beyond the gps_trace. This rider has not been making unsupported deviation claims.

Because the phantom line is the whole of the disputed SGD 2.00 and POL-RD-09(4) refunds such a line in full as a standalone correction, the entire contested amount is returned to the rider. On POL-GEN-03's party-relative vocabulary that is a full refund of the filing party's claim, together with a billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) which records the defect without suppressing the money.

POL-RD-01's numeric gate fails on this trip's own trace, so no deviation exists however the rider frames it. The measured excess is 0.18 km, or 4.6% of the 3.9 km optimal, and POL-RD-01 requires BOTH that the excess exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms AND that it exceed 20% of optimal before a deviation is ESTABLISHED. Neither limb is met, and POL-RD-01 says in terms that if either establishment test fails the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 expressly makes the trace figure govern: where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs and the trip record's rounded copy 'may NOT be cited for the threshold test'. The trace records 4.08 km over the 3.9 km optimal, and it is a clean measurement - 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s - so there is no reading of the record on which the excess approaches either threshold.

POL-RD-08 places the initial burden on the rider and requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold before the burden shifts to the driver. The rider has shown no such excess - 0.18 km and 4.6% - so the burden never shifts at all: the driver is never put to invoking POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12, and no exculpatory clause even needs to be reached.

fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 10.00, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run: no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the excess is characterised, and the rider is already whole on those lines. The rider's own words - 'ten dollar fixed price' - are the upfront quote, and under this fare model any detour cost falls on the driver, not on the rider.

Stripping the framing away, the whole contested sum is one ERP line and nothing else: charged_total 12.00 less quoted_fare 10.00 is exactly 2.00, and fare_breakdown.tolls_erp is 2.00, so there is no distance or time overcharge inside the contested amount at all. On an upfront trip POL-RD-11(a) leaves the rider only the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and no distance remedy attaches to the ROUTE_DEVIATION category on this record.

Nothing here fires a POL-RD-10 trigger, so the case is decidable on the record rather than escalatable: the trace meets POL-RD-07's integrity test (no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, cadence 10 s throughout, POL-RD-07 therefore not engaged); the trip identifier TRP-00521 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the timestamps run forward and agree; and the only unmatched charge line is the ERP line itself, which POL-RD-09(4) and POL-RD-10(8) both expressly exclude from the unmatched-line trigger.

The driver does not resist the 2.00 ERP line, and on this record cannot: the trace's closest approach to the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry is 6,778 m, far outside the 250 m POL-RD-09(4) crossing radius, so the line cannot stand as a crossed gantry and a 2.00 correction is due under POL-RD-09(4) - or equally under POL-RD-11(a)'s 'ERP actually crossed'. That correction is the ceiling and no more: it carries no distance or time refund, no POL-RD-06 uplift (there is no material deviation to uplift), and no escalation, because POL-RD-09(4) is a standalone billing-integrity correction and not a finding against the driver's routing on this trip.
